## Field constraints

The [`Field()`][pydantic.Field] function can also be used to add constraints to specific types:

```python
from decimal import Decimal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class Model(BaseModel):
    positive: int = Field(gt=0)
    short_str: str = Field(max_length=3)
    precise_decimal: Decimal = Field(max_digits=5, decimal_places=2)
```

The available constraints for each type (and the way they affect the JSON Schema) are described
in the [standard library types](../api/standard_library_types.md) documentation.

!!! note
    When adding constraints to a union type, if a member of the union is `None` or the [`MISSING` sentinel](./types.md#missing-sentinel),
    the constraints will be automatically applied to the remaining type(s) of the union:

    ```python
    from typing import Annotated

    from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


    class Model(BaseModel):
        positive: int | None = Field(gt=0)
        # Also works with the annotated pattern:
        negative: Annotated[int | None, Field(lt=0)]
    ```

request.instructions: The documents are sections of the documentation of ONE open-source project at one commit. Report a conflict only when two sections make incompatible statements about the SAME option, flag, default value, limit, version requirement, or behavior, for the same product version and scope. These are NOT conflicts: values of different options; example values in code samples that merely override a default; statements explicitly scoped to an older version or to migration history; one section giving more detail than the other; different defaults that the text ties to different contexts (per-route vs global, dev vs build, agent mode vs server mode).
